A 5-year-old boy presents to the pediatrician for a well child visit. He is meeting his developmental
milestones and is in the 15th percentile for height and 70th percentile for weight. His parents note that
he fatigues easily and has trouble participating in sports. They are concerned he is not getting enough
sleep and state that sometimes they hear him snore. The patient has a medical history of a
supracondylar fracture of the humerus, which was appropriately treated. He is doing well in school but
is sometimes bullied for being small. The patient eats a diet of milk, fruit, and some vegetables. His
temperature is 99.3°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 116/54 mmHg, pulse is 97/min, respirations are
20/min, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. On physical exam, the patient appears well. HEENT
exam is notable for conjunctival pallor and a unilateral clear middle ear effusion. Cardiac exam reveals
a benign flow murmur. Pulmonary exam is clear to auscultation bilaterally. The patient's gait is stable
and he is able to jump up and down. A full set of labs are ordered as requested by the parents including
a serum vitamin D level, B12 level, and IGF level. A selection of these lab values are seen
below:Serum:Na+: 139 mEq/L Cl-: 100 mEq/L K+: 4.3 mEq/L HCO3-: 25 mEq/LBUN: 20
mg/dLGlucose: 99 mg/dL Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL Ca2+: 9.9 mg/dL AST: 12 U/L ALT: 10 U/L Which of
the following would be found in this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Decreased total iron binding capacity
with normal ferritin (B) Normal RDW with decreased serum iron (C) Elevated reticulocyte count with

normal iron studies (D) Increased MCV (E) Decreased oxygen saturation when the patient sleeps (F)
Decreased serum ferritin with normal transferrin saturation (G) Decreased insulin-like growth factor
levels (H) Increased serum hepcidin levels (I) Increased RDW and TIBC (J) Microcytic anemia with
normal iron studies
 A. Elevated reticulocyte count with normal iron studies
B. Decreased insulin-like growth factor levels
C. Increased RDW and TIBC
D. Decreased total iron binding capacity with normal ferritin
E. Increased serum hepcidin levels
F. Microcytic anemia with normal iron studies
G. Increased MCV
H. Decreased oxygen saturation when the patient sleeps
I. Decreased serum ferritin with normal transferrin saturation
J. Normal RDW with decreased serum iron
